items.title: Add benchmark for building of decorators

items.body: ## Change Summary Part of https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/11975. `DecoratorInfos.build()` is currently implemented in a recursive way, and was doing more calls to itself than necessary. For instance, with the following: ```python from pydantic import BaseModel, computed_field class A(BaseModel): @computed_field def f(self) -> int: ... class B: @computed_field def g(self) -> int: ... class C(B): @computed_field def h(self) -> int: ... class D(A, C): pass ``` `DecoratorInfos` was building for the following classes: `B`, `C`, `B`, `A`, with a duplication of `B` because it is also present in the MRO of `c`. For classes that are not "owned" by Pydantic (bare classes, TypedDicts, stdlib dataclasses), we where also mutating these classes (setting the `__pydantic_decorators__` attribute, unwrapping decorators), which is pretty bad as these classes might come from third party libraries and be affected by these mutations. Setting the `__pydantic_decorators__` was done to avoid having to compute the `DecoratorInfos` instance again, so in theory this degrades performance but this is likely not an issue, see section below. --- While working on this, I came across the `Decorator.build()` implementation, computing references with `get_type_ref()` ([known to be slow](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/10863)) for every `build()` call (i.e. every decorator). I added a benchmark in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/12538, and can confirm this: In a follow-up PR, I'll try to find a way to optimize the ref computation (presumably we can easily leverage caching).

Reverts https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/11957.

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12413.

The reported flawed signature from the original issue was using the following signature: `(cls, values, info) -> ...`. However, https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/11957 resulted in the much more common (as per this [GH search](https://github.com/search?q=lang%3Apython+%2F%40model_validator%5C%28mode%3D%5B%27%22%5Dafter%5B%22%27%5D%5C%29%5Cs%2Bdef%5Cs.%2B%5C%28cls%2F&type=code)) `(cls, values) -> ...` signature (also not supposed to be accepted) to be confusingly broken (not rejected at build time, but the `values` argument is now the validation info).

According to [this comment](https://github.com/apache/iceberg-python/pull/2626#issuecomment-3407935823), the high usage of the invalid signature is probably due to V1 root validators changed to _after_ model validators, without changing from a class method to an instance method. As such, I updated the migration guide to mention this change.

This is a complete rewrite of the standard library types documentation page, which was seriously outdated, sometimes incorrect and with inconsistent markup.

The new version in this PR centralizes the information about validation, constraints (and how they affect JSON Schema), strictness, and serialization. It aims at being the single source of truth for information related to these types.

A new `union_format` parameter is added to the JSON Schema generation logic, defaulting `'any_of'` (the current behavior): ```python from typing import Annotated from pydantic import BaseModel, Field class Sub(BaseModel): ... class Model(BaseModel): a: int | None b: bool | str c: Annotated[str, Field(max_length=3)] | Annotated[str, Field(min_length=5)] d: list[int] | None e: Sub | None Model.model_json_schema(union_format='primitive_type_array') { │ '$defs': {'Sub': {'properties': {}, 'title': 'Sub', 'type': 'object'}}, │ 'properties': { │ │ 'a': {'title': 'A', 'type': ['integer', 'null']}, │ │ 'b': {'title': 'B', 'type': ['boolean', 'string']}, │ │ 'c': {'anyOf': [{'maxLength': 3, 'type': 'string'}, {'minLength': 5, 'type': 'string'}], 'title': 'C'}, │ │ 'd': {'anyOf': [{'items': {'type': 'integer'}, 'type': 'array'}, {'type': 'null'}], 'title': 'D'}, │ │ 'e': {'anyOf': [{'$ref': '#/$defs/Sub'}, {'type': 'null'}]} │ }, │ 'required': ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e'], │ 'title': 'Model', │ 'type': 'object' } ``` It only combines unions into a `type` array when using primitives (`string`, `boolean`, `null`, `integer` or `number`) _and_ when no metadata/constraints are used, otherwise fall backs to `anyOf`. We could also also apply this logic for non-primitives (e.g. arrays), but it can look a bit confusing depending on the tools consuming the JSON Schema. Taking [Swagger UI](https://swagger.io/tools/swagger-ui/) and [Redoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc): | JSON Schema | Swagger UI | Redoc | |--------|--------|--------| |[^1] | | | | [^2] | | | |[^3] | | | | [^4]| | | For this reason, I went with this `'primitive_type_array'` option. If we want to extend this in the future, we could add a new `'type_array'` option that would also use the type array form if non-primitive types are being used (although apart from `"array"` types, I'm not sure this will be really useful as most `"object"` types come from model/dataclasses/typeddicts, which are referenced types and wouldn't be inlined anyway). In the issue thread, it was mentioned to use `oneOf` as well, but I don't think it makes sense to make use of it (even if we are guaranteed that the union members are exclusive, such as ` | None`). `oneOf` means that it successfully validates if _one and only one_ member of the union validates, but this is not how Pydantic performs validation of union types. Depending on the [union mode](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/unions/#union-modes), union members are validated differently but in all cases there is no constraint that it should only validate against only one member. A new union member could be introduced to do so (and then it would make sense to generate a `oneOf` schema for it), but this wasn't requested so far because the use case is pretty niche. --- I'll also note that FastAPI currently does _not_ support `type` arrays. The fix might be as simple as changing the [`Schema.type` definition](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/blob/6df50d40fe195adc026af169d6ebf298a1c183a5/fastapi/openapi/models.py#L160) from `str | None` to `str | list[str] | None`, but there might be other things to consider. Reported in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/12787. [^1]: `{"type": ["array", "string"], "items": {"type": "string"}}` [^2]: `{"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}]}` [^3]: `{"type": ["object", "string"], "properties": {"f": {"type": "string"}}}` [^4]: `{"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "object", "properties": {"f": {"type": "string"}}}]}`
